extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent owners / patent practitioners participating in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, filing, and evaluating responses (including amendments, supplemental replies, and service) to Office actions in ex parte reexamination proceedings under the MPEP and 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reply to adverse Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office action after the first examination (§ 1.104) is adverse in any respect, the applicant or patent owner, if he or she persists in his or her application for a patent or reexamination proceeding, must reply and request reconsideration or further examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §§ 1.135 and 1.136 for time for reply to avoid abandonment. This reply requirement applies to reexamination proceedings per 37 CFR 1.550(a) (except that 1.136 time‑to‑reply provisions do not apply to reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies restricted and not a matter of right
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply that is supplemental to a reply that is in compliance with § 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except as provided in paragraph (a)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may enter a supplemental reply only if it is clearly limited to: (A) Cancellation of a claim(s); (B) Adoption of the examiner suggestion(s); (C) Placement of the application in condition for allowance; (D) Reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; (E) Correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); or (F) Simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply will be entered if filed during the period when action by the Office is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c). If a supplemental reply is not approved for entry, its contents must be included in a proper response to a subsequent Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies must distinctly and specifically point out errors and address every ground
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply must be reduced to a writing which distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out the specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over any applied references. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifically pointing out how the language of the claims patentably distinguishes them from the references does not comply with this requirement. The reply must appear throughout to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must show patentable novelty and avoidance of references
rubrics_metrics.description: In amending in reply to a rejection of claims in an application or patent under reexamination, the applicant or patent owner must clearly point out the patentable novelty which he or she thinks the claims present in view of the state of the art disclosed by the references cited or the objections made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant or patent owner must also show how the amendments avoid such references or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner minimum response period and content options
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be given at least thirty days to respond to any Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In response to any rejection, such response may include further statements and/or proposed amendments or new claims to place the patent in a condition where all claims, if amended as proposed, would be patentable. The patent owner is required to serve a copy of any response made in the reexamination proceeding on the third party requester (37 CFR 1.550(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time are limited and require petitions/fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for taking any action by a patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding may be extended as provided in specific rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for an extension must specify the requested period and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g). For third party requested reexamination, extension requests must be filed on or before the day action is due and will not be granted in the absence of sufficient cause or for more than a reasonable time. For patent owner requested or Director ordered reexamination, extensions up to two months have specific filing deadlines; extensions for more than two months are tightly restricted. In any event, a reply must be filed prior to the expiration of the period of extension and never later than the maximum statute‑set period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file timely and appropriate response terminates prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any written statement of an interview required under § 1.560(b), the prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon termination the Director will proceed to issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination proceeding under § 1.570. A petition under § 1.137 may be filed to revive a prosecution terminated for unintentional delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party requester receives copies and service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination requester will be sent copies of Office actions issued during the ex parte reexamination proceeding; after filing of a request by a third party, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document must reflect service or the document may be refused consideration by the Office. Proof of service (certificate of service) must be attached to the paper; the certificate must set forth name and address of party served and method of service. Missing proof of service may result in denial of consideration or issuance of a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL‑475). See MPEP § 2266.03 for full service procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party requester participation ends with reply; restrictions on further third‑party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535, and no further submissions on behalf of the reexamination requester will be acknowledged or considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further third‑party submissions will not be considered unless they are in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535, or were entered in the patent file prior to the date of the order for reexamination pursuant to § 1.525. Submissions by third parties filed after the order must meet the requirements of § 1.501(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirements for reexamination petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.20(c)(6) except for certain enumerated petition types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include petitions to extend the period for response by a patent owner under paragraph (c), petitions under paragraph (e) to accept a delayed response by a patent owner, petitions under § 1.78 for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim, and petitions under § 1.530(l) for correction of inventorship in a reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing/transmission and Priority Mail Express use allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and certificate of transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8), and the Priority Mail Express® mailing procedure (37 CFR 1.10), may be used to file any response in a pending ex parte reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are approved methods for filing responses and establish proving the filing date under the applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing papers on behalf of third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must not file papers on behalf of a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a third party paper accompanies, or is submitted as part of a timely filed response, the response and the third party paper are considered an improper submission and the entire submission shall be returned to the patent owner; the third party paper will not be considered. The returning decision should provide an appropriate extension of time if prior to final rejection to refile without the third party paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) generally not permitted in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner cannot submit an application data sheet (ADS) in a reexamination proceeding except as provided in MPEP § 2258.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADS submission rules are restricted in the reexamination context and must follow the specified MPEP provision when permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'not fully responsive' to a non‑final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: A response by the patent owner will be considered not fully responsive where: (A) a bona fide response to an examiner’s non‑final action is filed; (B) before the expiration of the permissible response period (including any extensions); and (C) through apparent oversight or inadvertence, some point necessary to a full response has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition triggers special handling (see related examiner options) and is limited to inadvertent omissions, not deliberate ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner options for 'not fully responsive' submissions prior to final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent owner submission prior to final rejection is not fully responsive and meets (A)-(C), the examiner may: (A) waive the deficiencies (if not serious) and act on the submission; (B) accept the amendment as a response but notify the patent owner via a new Office action that the omission must be supplied; or (C) notify the patent owner that the response must be completed within the remaining period for response (or within any extension) to avoid termination of the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The third alternative should be used only in very unusual situations where sufficient time remains. Form paragraph 22.14 may be used where a bona fide response is not entirely responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of minor deficiencies in otherwise bona fide responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission responds to the rejections, objections, or requirements and is a bona fide attempt to advance, but contains a minor deficiency (e.g., fails to treat every rejection, objection, or requirement), the examiner may simply act on the amendment and issue a new (non‑final or final) Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new Office action may reiterate the unaddressed rejection/objection or indicate it is no longer applicable, and must identify the part of the previous Office action not responded to and make clear what is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of serious deficiencies and timing considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission contains a serious deficiency to be dealt with prior to issuing an action on the merits and the period for response has expired, or there is insufficient time remaining to correct before expiration, the patent owner should be notified of the deficiency and given a new time period for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner must supply the omission within the new time period (or extensions) to avoid termination. The patent owner may also file a further response as permitted under § 1.111. Examiner discretion applies; but be mindful of substantial patent rights and lack of refiling opportunities. If the amendment would place the proceeding in condition for issuance except for an omission through oversight, the examiner should consider entering the response, withdrawing the final action, and issuing a new Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.14 usage and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.14 may be used where a bona fide response is not entirely responsive to a non‑final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form text explains that the communication appears bona fide but omitted necessary matter; sets a shortened statutory period to supply omission; examiner notes instruct specific bracketed content (e.g., explain omitted point, set period as ONE MONTH or two months depending on requester). This paragraph is only used for pre‑final responses; after final rejection advisory actions are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent omission doctrine and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving the patent owner time to supply an omission applies only when the missing matter or lack of compliance is considered by the examiner as being 'inadvertently omitted' and does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an inadvertent omission is brought to the patent owner’s attention, inadvertence no longer exists and a second Office action giving another new time period would not be appropriate (except in limited, different‑issue circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Different practice after final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving a new time period to supply an omission does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide response filed after final rejection omits a necessary point, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond; rather, an advisory Office action (form PTOL‑467) should be issued explaining the omission. The time in the final rejection continues to run and is extended by two months if the response is the first after final under guidelines in MPEP § 2265. Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate or are in better form for appeal; otherwise denied entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner authority regarding entry and withdrawal of final action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner has authority to enter the response, withdraw the final Office action, and issue a new Office action where appropriate (Ex parte Quayle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is within examiner discretion, but examiners should recognize substantial patent rights and lack of refiling opportunities; where time has expired for response and the amendment would place the proceeding in condition for issuance except for an omission through oversight, the examiner should follow this course of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects rendering a submission an 'informal submission' (defective paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the substance of a submission is complete, the submission can be defective (an 'informal submission'). Examples: (A) The paper filed does not include proof of service; (B) The paper filed is unsigned; (C) The paper filed is signed by a non‑practitioner who is not of record; (D) The amendment filed by the patent owner does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) The amendment filed by the patent owner does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or 1.20(c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is defective prior to final rejection, use forms PTOL‑475 or PTO‑2311 to notify the defect and set a time period to correct; extensions may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). If the defect is not corrected, the submission will not be entered and may lead to termination if it results in failure to file a timely appropriate response. If a defective response is filed after final rejection, issue an advisory Office action (PTOL‑467) explaining the informality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTOL‑475 / PTO‑2311 for notifying defective papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission made prior to final rejection is defective (informal), forms PTOL‑475 and PTO‑2311 are used to provide notification of the defects present in the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL‑475 provides notification for a third‑party requested reexamination; PTO‑2311 for patent owner requested or Director ordered reexamination. Often only boxes are checked; additional clarification may be attached on a separate sheet if specifics are needed. The 'other' box may be used for defects not listed on the form (e.g., submission on easily erasable paper). A time period from the mailing date will be set for correction. If not corrected, submission will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers requirements and consequences of failure to serve
rubrics_metrics.description: Any paper filed with the Office in a third party requested reexamination must be served on every other party in the reexamination proceeding and be accompanied by a certificate of service setting forth the name and address of the party served and the method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the certificate of service must also be attached with the copy served on the other party. Papers filed without proof of service may be denied consideration. If service was inadvertently omitted but actually made, the filer should submit a supplemental paper indicating manner and date of service and the submission should be entered with annotation 'Service confirmed by [name] on [date]'. If no service was made or the filer cannot be contacted, the submission is usually not considered and is placed in the IFW file history as an unentered paper with notation 'N/E' and 'no service'. A Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL‑475) giving one month or thirty days (whichever longer) to complete the paper will generally be mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.15 for lack of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.15 may be used to give notice where a submission appears not to have been served as required in a third party requester reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph text notifies the filer that the submission is defective for lack of service and requires proper service and certificate within a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, from the mailing date. Examiner notes indicate bracketed insertions (e.g., insert 'patent owner' or 'third party requester'). Use PTOL‑473 as the cover sheet for mailing the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to serve submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure of a party to serve the submission in response to the notice will have consequences: (A) For a patent owner statement or a third party reply, the submission may be refused consideration by the Office; (B) For a patent owner response to an Office action, the response may be refused consideration and prosecution may be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless the patent owner has otherwise completely responded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special handling applies if missing service affects a response to a final rejection (use advisory Office action rather than PTOL‑475/22.15). See MPEP §§ 2220, 2249, 2251, and 2266 for related procedures and documents.
